s: Module 3 Part IV — Site Planning & Land Use
q: What is a permeable rock or soil layer that can store and yield significant groundwater?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: An aquifer holds and transmits groundwater; the water table is only the top surface of the saturated zone.

s: Module 3 Part I — Interior Design & Ergonomics
q: Which discipline studies how people interact with the other parts of a system to improve well-being and performance?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Ergonomics (human factors) fits the system to the person; anthropometry only supplies the body measurements it uses.

s: Module 3 Part IV — Site Planning & Land Use
q: On an urban land-use map, what color are the industrial zones I-1, I-2 and I-3?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Industrial uses are violet; residential is yellow, commercial red and institutional blue.

s: Module 3 Part I — Interior Design & Ergonomics
q: What is the standard depth of a kitchen counter?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: A 600 mm counter fits standard base cabinets and appliances with room to work in front of the backsplash.

s: Module 3 Part IV — Site Planning & Land Use
q: In choosing a site for a commercial development, what should come first?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Shops and offices live on being seen and reached, so visibility and access outrank the shape or size of the lot.

s: Module 3 Part II — Landscape Architecture
q: Which field designs outdoor areas, landmarks and structures for environmental, social or aesthetic ends?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Landscape architecture shapes outdoor space; horticulture is the growing of plants, and urban planning works at the scale of the city.

s: Module 3 Part IV — Site Planning & Land Use
q: Which location is least suitable for a high-end restaurant that serves liquor?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Liquor-serving outlets are restricted near schools, and a school crowd is the wrong market for a high-end restaurant.

s: Module 3 Part II — Landscape Architecture
q: Who is called the Father of Philippine Landscape Architecture?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: IP Santos pioneered the profession in the Philippines and was named National Artist for Architecture in 2006; Olmsted holds the title for the United States.

s: Module 3 Part IV — Site Planning & Land Use
q: A beachfront site in Palawan faces west over the sea. What must the design control while keeping the view open?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: A west-facing sea view brings low, hot afternoon sun and glare off the water, so shading must be designed without blocking the view.

s: Module 3 Part II — Landscape Architecture
q: Which of these is NOT a softscape element?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Softscape is the living material; pavers are hardscape.

s: Short Quiz 3 — Interior & Landscape Design
q: According to WHO data, what is the average height of Filipino men?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Adult Filipino men average about 163 cm, roughly 5 ft 4 in.

s: Module 3 Part II — Landscape Architecture
q: Which trees suit the garden of a 4 m high bungalow?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Small trees stay in scale with a low house and keep roots and branches clear of the roof and foundation.

s: Short Quiz 3 — Interior & Landscape Design
q: What is the psychological effect usually linked to the color red?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Red raises alertness and energy; blues and greens are the calming colors.

s: Module 3 Part II — Landscape Architecture
q: Which French formal garden did André Le Nôtre lay out, one of the largest gardens ever made?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Le Nôtre's gardens at Versailles, about 800 ha, are the model French formal garden; Giverny is Monet's.

s: Short Quiz 3 — Interior & Landscape Design
q: What is the standard size of a queen-size bed?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: A queen is 60 × 80 in; 54 × 75 is a full (double) and 76 × 80 a king.

s: Module 3 Part II — Landscape Architecture
q: What is a frame of latticework used as a screen or as a support for climbing plants?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: A trellis is a flat lattice; a pergola is a post-and-beam structure over a walk, and a gazebo a roofed pavilion.

s: Short Quiz 3 — Interior & Landscape Design
q: Which palm leaf is the national leaf of the Philippines?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: The anahaw (Livistona rotundifolia) is a fan palm that grows to about 20 m; its round leaves are used for thatch and fans.

s: Module 3 Part II — Landscape Architecture
q: What do you call a walk bordered by trees or clipped hedges in a garden, park or street?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: An allée is a path lined by trees or tall hedges; pleaching is a way of weaving the branches.

s: Short Quiz 3 — Interior & Landscape Design
q: What is the non-living part of a landscape, such as stone walls, brick patios and tiled paths?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Hardscape is the built, inanimate part of a landscape; softscape is the planting.

s: Module 3 Part II — Landscape Architecture
q: A tree is moved by digging around it in a circle so most of its roots stay in a ball of soil. What is this called?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Root balling keeps the roots in their soil, wrapped for the move, so the tree survives transplanting.

s: Short Quiz 4 — Site Planning Principles
q: What is the art of arranging structures on the land and shaping the spaces between them?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Kevin Lynch's definition: site planning arranges buildings and the spaces between; site analysis only studies the site first.

s: Module 3 Part III — Tropical Design & Passive Cooling
q: What type of climate does the Philippines have?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: The Philippines is tropical maritime: hot, humid and rainy, with small daily and yearly temperature swings.

s: Short Quiz 4 — Site Planning Principles
q: Which design approach controls heat gain and sheds heat to keep interiors comfortable with little or no energy?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Passive cooling uses shading, ventilation and mass instead of machines; active cooling uses mechanical plant.

s: Module 3 Part III — Tropical Design & Passive Cooling
q: Which of these does NOT describe the Philippine climate?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Philippine air is humid most of the year; dry air belongs to hot-arid climates.

s: Short Quiz 4 — Site Planning Principles
q: What is the number of people per unit of land area called?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Population density is people per km² or per hectare; distribution is where they are located.

s: Module 3 Part III — Tropical Design & Passive Cooling
q: Which side of a building takes the hottest afternoon sun?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: The low afternoon sun strikes the west walls just as the air is hottest.

s: Short Quiz 4 — Site Planning Principles
q: On a land-use map, what color is a zone of bungalows and other houses?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Residential land is yellow.

s: Module 3 Part III — Tropical Design & Passive Cooling
q: Which sides of a building are best shaded by horizontal sunshades, because the sun reaches them from high up?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: High-angle sun on north and south faces is cut by overhangs; low east and west sun needs vertical fins.

s: Short Quiz 4 — Site Planning Principles
q: Which is a correct principle of air movement?
o: Air flows from high pressure to low pressure
Air flows from low pressure to high pressure
Air takes the path of most resistance
Air flows at a steady speed everywhere
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Pressure difference drives airflow, and air follows the path of least resistance.

s: Module 3 Part III — Tropical Design & Passive Cooling
q: What does the French term brise-soleil mean?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: A brise-soleil is a fixed sun-breaking screen of fins or louvers; an egg-crate is one form of it.

s: Module 3 Part I — Interior Design & Ergonomics
q: Which element of interior design, natural or artificial, most sets the mood of a space?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Light reveals every other element, so it sets the mood; color and texture depend on it.

s: Module 3 Part III — Tropical Design & Passive Cooling
q: What is the upwind side of a building called?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Windward faces the wind and takes positive pressure; leeward is the sheltered, downwind side.

s: Module 3 Part I — Interior Design & Ergonomics
q: A track light aimed at artwork is an example of what kind of lighting?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Accent light picks out one object; ambient or general light fills the whole room.

s: Module 3 Part III — Tropical Design & Passive Cooling
q: Which Philippine stilt house, of light framing and nipa, has large awning windows for cross ventilation and shade?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: The bahay kubo is the lowland nipa hut; the bahay na bato adds a stone ground floor.

s: Module 3 Part I — Interior Design & Ergonomics
q: What kind of light defines Tadao Ando's Church of the Light, entering through a cross cut in the concrete behind the altar?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Daylight through the cut cross is the only ornament; the space is defined by sunlight against solid concrete.

s: Module 3 Part IV — Site Planning & Land Use
q: What is the solid, consolidated rock beneath the soil and gravel called?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Bedrock is the continuous solid rock under the loose surface layers; hardpan is only a compacted soil layer.

s: Module 3 Part I — Interior Design & Ergonomics
q: Which color is the complement of orange?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Complements sit opposite on the color wheel: orange is across from blue.

s: Module 3 Part IV — Site Planning & Land Use
q: Which is NOT a usual problem of a steep site?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Water runs off steep ground fast, so ponding and flooding are problems of flat sites instead.

s: Module 3 Part I — Interior Design & Ergonomics
q: Which of these is NOT one of the three properties of a color?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Hue, value and saturation (chroma) are the properties; a tint is what you get by adding white.

s: Module 3 Part IV — Site Planning & Land Use
q: What slope is usually taken as optimum for a housing site?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: About 2% drains well without making streets or lots awkward; below 1% drains poorly.

s: Module 3 Part I — Interior Design & Ergonomics
q: What is the study of measurements of the human body?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Anthropometry measures the body; ergonomics applies those measures to design.

s: Module 3 Part IV — Site Planning & Land Use
q: What is the land area where precipitation collects and drains to a common outlet such as a river or bay?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: A watershed, or drainage basin, is bounded by ridges and drains to one outlet.

s: Module 3 Part I — Interior Design & Ergonomics
q: What is the comfortable reach range for overhead cabinets and high storage?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Most adults reach shelves between about 1.5 and 1.7 m without a step.

s: Module 3 Part IV — Site Planning & Land Use
q: On an urban land-use map, what color are the TZ zones?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: TZ zones are shown in orange on the land-use color code.

s: Module 3 Part I — Interior Design & Ergonomics
q: What is the size of a standard king mattress (Asian standard)?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: The Asian king is 72 × 75 in; 60 × 75 is a queen and 54 × 75 a double.

s: Module 3 Part IV — Site Planning & Land Use
q: Which lot type is least desirable for a public school?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: A corner through lot has streets on three sides, exposing the pupils to traffic and noise all around.

s: Module 3 Part II — Landscape Architecture
q: Which 340-hectare Manhattan park was one of the first American parks shaped by landscape architecture?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Olmsted and Vaux designed Central Park from 1858.

s: Module 3 Part IV — Site Planning & Land Use
q: Which site factor must be checked for its availability, adequacy and efficiency on site?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Water, power, drainage and sewer lines must reach the site with enough capacity before design commits to it.

s: Module 3 Part II — Landscape Architecture
q: Which 58-hectare park in Ermita, Manila, is among the notable works of IP Santos?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: IP Santos worked on the Luneta, one of the largest urban parks in Asia.

s: Module 3 Part IV — Site Planning & Land Use
q: For a Palawan site facing the beach, what should the design make the most of?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: The sea view is the main value of such a site, so rooms and openings are arranged to capture it.

s: Module 3 Part II — Landscape Architecture
q: Which of these trees is deciduous?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Molave sheds its leaves in the dry season; pine and ilang-ilang keep them all year.

s: Short Quiz 3 — Interior & Landscape Design
q: According to WHO data, what is the average height of Filipino women?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Adult Filipino women average about 150 cm, roughly 4 ft 11 in.

s: Module 3 Part II — Landscape Architecture
q: In landscape design, shrubs are plants of about what height range?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Shrubs sit between groundcovers (under 50 cm) and trees (4 m and up).

s: Short Quiz 3 — Interior & Landscape Design
q: Which property of color tells its brightness or dullness?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Intensity (saturation) is how pure or dull a color is; value is how light or dark.

s: Module 3 Part II — Landscape Architecture
q: Which of these is NOT a hardscape element?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: A lawn is living ground cover, so it is softscape.

s: Short Quiz 3 — Interior & Landscape Design
q: What is a planned outdoor space, usually large and open to the public?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: A park is large and public; a garden is usually smaller and focused on plants.

s: Module 3 Part II — Landscape Architecture
q: What is a fence or boundary formed by closely planted shrubs?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: A hedge is a living boundary; a palisade is a fence of stakes, and a green wall is planting on a wall.

s: Short Quiz 3 — Interior & Landscape Design
q: What is a park within a city that gives residents and visitors green space for recreation?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: An urban park serves a city; national parks protect large natural areas.

s: Module 3 Part II — Landscape Architecture
q: Which of these is NOT a waterscape feature?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: A jet nozzle is a fitting inside a fountain, not a water feature by itself.

s: Short Quiz 3 — Interior & Landscape Design
q: Which garden tradition uses clipped hedges, geometric beds and a strong axis, as at Versailles?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: The French formal garden imposes geometry on nature; the English garden imitates it.

s: Module 3 Part III — Tropical Design & Passive Cooling
q: What is a garden structure of posts carrying beams or lattice that forms a shaded walk or sitting area?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: A pergola is a post-and-beam frame over a walk; an arbor is a small arch, a gazebo a roofed pavilion.

s: Short Quiz 4 — Site Planning Principles
q: Which design approach uses planning and design to keep interiors cool despite a hot and humid climate?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Tropical design answers heat, humidity and rain through orientation, shading and ventilation.

s: Module 3 Part III — Tropical Design & Passive Cooling
q: Which climatic element need NOT be considered in a tropical country?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Snow never falls in the lowland tropics; sun, wind and rain drive tropical design.

s: Short Quiz 4 — Site Planning Principles
q: What is a scene seen from a vantage point called?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: A view is any scene seen from a point; a vista is a view framed down a corridor, and a panorama a wide sweep.

s: Module 3 Part III — Tropical Design & Passive Cooling
q: Which season is dominated by the cool northeast trade winds, with mild temperatures and little rain?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: The Amihan (northeast monsoon) runs from about October to March; the Habagat is the rainy southwest monsoon.

s: Short Quiz 4 — Site Planning Principles
q: Which tool identifies the passive cooling strategy suited to a building site?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Olgyay's bioclimatic chart plots temperature against humidity to show which strategy restores comfort.

s: Module 3 Part III — Tropical Design & Passive Cooling
q: Which side of a building in the Philippines can take full-height glazing?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: At about 14°N the sun stays mostly to the south, so north glass gets steady daylight with little direct sun.

s: Short Quiz 4 — Site Planning Principles
q: What is the upper boundary of the zone of groundwater called?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: The water table is the top of the saturated zone; below it the ground is full of water.

s: Module 3 Part III — Tropical Design & Passive Cooling
q: Which sides of a building are best shaded by vertical fins?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Vertical fins block the low, side-angled morning and afternoon sun on east and west faces.

s: Short Quiz 4 — Site Planning Principles
q: In the Philippines, what is the Habagat?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: The Habagat brings rain from the southwest from about June to September; the Amihan is the northeast monsoon.

s: Module 3 Part III — Tropical Design & Passive Cooling
q: Where should the full-height window of a master's bedroom face in the Philippines?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: North glass gives daylight without the hot afternoon sun of the west or the direct sun on the south.

s: Module 3 Part I — Interior Design & Ergonomics
q: Which type of light is meant to highlight a particular piece?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Accent light focuses on one object; task light serves an activity.

s: Module 3 Part III — Tropical Design & Passive Cooling
q: If mechanical cooling is unavoidable in a tropical building, which system adjusts its refrigerant flow to each zone's load?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: VRF varies compressor speed and refrigerant flow zone by zone, so it wastes little energy at part load.

s: Module 3 Part I — Interior Design & Ergonomics
q: A desk lamp is an example of what kind of lighting?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Task light lights a specific activity such as reading or writing.

s: Module 3 Part III — Tropical Design & Passive Cooling
q: Which Philippine ancestral house stands on a stone ground floor, with large windows and ventanillas for cross ventilation?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: The bahay na bato puts a timber upper floor on a stone base, with sliding capiz windows and ventanillas.

s: Module 3 Part I — Interior Design & Ergonomics
q: Which are the secondary colors?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Secondaries come from mixing two primaries: yellow + blue = green, red + yellow = orange, red + blue = violet.

s: Module 3 Part IV — Site Planning & Land Use
q: Which is the usual problem of a flat site?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Water ponds on flat ground that falls less than about 1%, so drainage is the main problem.

s: Module 3 Part I — Interior Design & Ergonomics
q: Which two colors form a split-complementary scheme with yellow?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Yellow's complement is violet; a split complementary uses the two hues on either side of it.

s: Module 3 Part IV — Site Planning & Land Use
q: What slope is usually taken as optimum for a playground?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Play areas are kept nearly flat, about 1%, just enough to drain.

s: Module 3 Part I — Interior Design & Ergonomics
q: Which color makes a space soothing, luminous and friendly, less showy than red?
ref: Theory of architecture: site planning, landscape, tropical and interior design
n: Orange keeps the warmth of red with less intensity, giving a friendly, glowing space.
